title: Quantum Noncommutativity Uniquely Determines Relative Entropy
summary: Quantum relative entropy is a core concept in physics, governing the limits of communication, thermodynamic irreversibility and quantum resource conversion. However, the requirement that physical processes cannot increase state distinguishability, the data-processing inequality, permits an infinite family of alternative divergence measures. Here we show that quantum relative entropy is uniquely selected by a sharper operational principle.
